name: Blokus
edition: Blokus (classic) instruction sheet R1983, 2008 design, file R1983-0825

setup.text: Place the 20 by 20 board between you.
Each player picks a colour and puts its 21 pieces at their side of the board. Turn order is blue, yellow, red, green.

by_count.2: Each player takes two colours: one gets blue and red, the other yellow and green.
by_count.3: Each player takes one colour. The fourth colour is shared and played in turn by all three.

setup.text: Blue goes first, then yellow, red and green. Your first piece must cover one of the board's corner squares.

turn.summary: Place one of your pieces on the board so it touches your own pieces only at a corner.
steps: Choose one of your remaining pieces and place it on the board.
Your first piece must cover a corner square of the board.
Each later piece must touch at least one of your own pieces at a corner only, never along an edge.
Pieces of different colours may touch in any way, and a placed piece cannot be moved.
With two players, play your two colours in the turn order. With three, one player after another also plays the shared colour in its turn.

end: The game ends when no player can lay down any more pieces, including players who have placed all of theirs.

scoring.text: Count the unit squares in your unplaced pieces: each is minus 1 point.
Plus 15 if all your pieces are on the board, and plus 5 more if your last piece was the single-square piece.
With two players, add the scores of your two colours. With three players, ignore the shared colour's score.

missed.text: Same-colour pieces may touch only at corners; edge contact is not allowed. Other colours have no such limit.
The 5-point bonus only counts if the single square is the last piece you place.
Unplaced squares cost one point each, so try to dump your big pieces early.
In the four-player game the order is blue, yellow, red, green, whatever the seating.
In a three-player game the shared colour is played alternately by each player, and its score is ignored.

unverified: The sheet does not say outright what happens on the turn of a player who cannot place a piece; entry treats them as blocked, with play continuing until everyone is blocked.
